title: Capacity resilience: failure modes, graceful fallback, and auditability for reserved pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD defining required behavior when reserved capacity pools experience degradations or transient shortages. Covers deterministic fallback routing, rapid tenant isolation when noisy neighbors affect latency, audit trails for capacity decisions, and clear acceptance criteria for safe autoscale and prewarm operations. The intent is to ensure customer workloads degrade gracefully, operators have actionable telemetry and audit logs, and billing and SLOs remain explainable during incidents.
problem_statement: Reserved pools can suffer from transient hotspots, failed prewarm jobs, or mis-sized allocations. Without explicit fallback rules and auditability, customer traffic can experience opaque errors, silent latency spikes, or billing anomalies. Engineering and SRE teams currently lack runbooks that tie capacity events to automated fallbacks and post-incident accounting.
goals: Define deterministic fallback policy: how requests move from reserved pool -> soft-reserve overflow -> burst reservoir -> best-effort public capacity
Provide tenant-level isolation controls that limit blast radius of noisy jobs while preserving minimum throughput for critical tenants
Emit structured audit logs for capacity decisions with enough context for billing reconciliation and postmortems
Add acceptance tests and dashboards that validate graceful degradation of p99 latency and error budget behavior during overload
Ensure fallback decisions are explainable in Console and surfaced in customer-facing incidents
non_goals: Re-architecting global scheduler in this PRD
Building new billing pipeline (we will add tags/events consumed by billing team but not change billing infra)
Full RBAC for audit search (search UX improvements queued separately)
success_metrics: During simulated 30-minute MTTD test, p99 latency for reserved tenants must not increase > 2x baseline after fallback is engaged
Audit log completeness: >= 95% of fallback decisions include request_id, tenant_id, pool_id, trigger_reason, and chosen_destination
False-positive isolation events < 1% during chaos tests
Post-incident customer tickets attributable to opaque capacity behavior reduced by 60% in the first quarter after launch
user_stories: As a platform SRE, I want deterministic rules so I can quickly reason about where traffic went during shortage
As a PM for a high-priority tenant, I want guaranteed minimal throughput (soft SLO) even if other tenants spike
As a billing analyst, I want audit events tied to capacity routing that I can join to usage records for reconciliation
As an on-call engineer, I want Circuit Breaker hooks that notify me when prewarm failures cause fallback so I can investigate
requirements: Fallback policy engine: implement policy DSL that expresses ordered destinations with capacity weights and eviction priority
Isolation controller: per-tenant rate shaping + soft-minimum allocation that the runtime honors under overload
Audit schema: JSON events emitted to existing event bus with fields: timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, pool_id, trigger, chosen_pool, prev_pool, reason_code, snapshot_of_pool_utilization
Observability: dashboard and SLO checks for fallback counts, mean time to fallback recovery, and p99 latency per tenant
Testing harness: deterministic chaos tests to simulate prewarm failure, node crash, and sudden 5x traffic burst
Operator playbook: runbook mapping reason_code -> remediation steps and escalation path
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for fallback policy DSL with coverage of priority ordering and weight changes
E2E chaos run: deploy to staging, trigger prewarm failure, validate that fallback routing occurred and audit events were emitted for >= 98% of affected requests
Console surfaces a human-friendly explanation for each fallback event (tenant view) that includes the reason_code and fallback timestamp
Isolation controller respects tenant soft-min: during a controlled noisy neighbor test, critical tenant retains >= 70% of baseline throughput while noisy tenant is throttled
Audit events are ingested into the event pipeline and match sample schema; billing team confirms joinable keys for reconciliation
Operator playbook validated in tabletop exercise with on-call responding within defined SLAs
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement policy engine + audit events in staging and validate with synthetic load (1 sprint). Phase 2: Canary in a small set of Dedicated pools with low-risk tenants and explicit invites (2 sprints). Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% of reserved pools with monitoring thresholds for rollback. Phase 4: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy ad-hoc fallbacks.
risks: Incorrect weighting in fallback could starve smaller tenants if policy testing is insufficient
Audit event volume could increase event bus costs if not sampled or batched
Operator confusion if reason_codes are not human-friendly; risk of delayed remediation
Rollback complexity if policy changes have to be reverted quickly during a live incident
decisions: Use existing event bus for audit events rather than introducing a new pipeline
Implement policy DSL that is intentionally conservative (prefer soft-throttling before eviction)
Expose fallback counts and last-fallback timestamp in Console tenant detail page
notes: Work with billing to add 'fallback_tag' to usage records for reconciliation
SRE prefers a small set of reason_codes initially: PREWARM_FAIL, POOL_EXHAUST, NODE_CRASH, QoS_VIOLATION
Keep audit payload under 2KB per event; prefer pointer to snapshot stored in object store for large pool metrics
